subject.title: Azure OpenAI Responses throws 400 when prompt_cache_key is sent to endpoints that do not support it

question: Should Azure OpenAI Responses keep sending `prompt_cache_key` by default for native Azure routes, or should Azure prompt-cache hints require explicit support or opt-in?
rationale: The code path is clear, but changing the default trades endpoint compatibility against cache affinity and would reverse current tests/docs without live proof of the rejecting Azure route.

options.title: Request live Azure proof first
options.body: Ask for the deployment, model, API version, and redacted 400 body before changing the default behavior.

options.title: Keep default with documented opt-out
options.body: Keep native Azure prompt-cache hints by default and direct affected users to `cacheRetention: "none"` or an explicit compat opt-out when their endpoint rejects the field.

options.title: Make Azure cache hints opt-in
options.body: Stop sending Azure prompt-cache fields unless config or capability detection explicitly declares support, reducing 400s while changing tested native-route behavior.

recommendation.title: Request live Azure proof first
recommendation.body: Ask for the deployment, model, API version, and redacted 400 body before changing the default behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history on the Azure provider package split, prompt-cache docs, and payload-builder lines.
